title: Euclid preparation. Non-Gaussianity of 2-pt statistics likelihood: Parameter inference with a non-Gaussian likelihood in Fourier and configuration space
summary: In this work we account for this skewness in parameter inference by modelling the likelihood through an Edgeworth expansion which involves the complete skewness tensor, composed of 1-point, 2-point, and 3-point correlators. To simplify the calculations of this expansion we perform a change of basis which reduces the precision matrix to the identity. In this basis, the off-diagonal elements of the skewness tensor are consistent with zero, while the amplitude of its diagonal match the level expected for a Gaussian underlying field. We perform parameter inference with this likelihood model and find that including only the diagonal part of the skewness is sufficient, while incorporating the full skewness tensor injects noise without improving accuracy. Despite the estimated excess skewness in the original basis, the cosmological constraints remain effectively unchanged when adopting a Gaussian likelihood or considering the more complete Edgeworth expansion, with variations in the figure of merit of cosmological parameters between the two cases below $5\%$. This result remains unchanged against variations of the survey volume and geometry, scale-cut, and 2-point statistic (power spectrum or correlation function). Using $10\, 000$ cloned \Euclid large mocks based on realistic galaxy catalogues with characteristics close to future \Euclid data, we find no detectable excess skewness on intermediate scales, due to the level of shot noise expected for the \Euclid spectroscopic sample. We conclude that the Gaussian likelihood assumption is robust for \Euclid 2-point statistics analyses in both Fourier and configuration space.

AI.tldr: This study shows that skewness in likelihood has minimal impact on cosmological parameter inference with Euclid-like data; Gaussian likelihood assumptions are confirmed robust using Edgeworth expansion and extensive mock catalogs.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the issue of skewness in parameter inference and its impact on cosmological constraints, aiming to improve likelihood modeling beyond the Gaussian assumption.
AI.method: They model the likelihood using an Edgeworth expansion incorporating the full skewness tensor (1-point, 2-point, 3-point correlators). A change of basis simplifies the precision matrix and skewness tensor computations, focusing on diagonal terms.
AI.result: Including only the diagonal skewness terms suffices; full skewness tensor inclusion adds noise without accuracy gains. Cosmological constraints remain nearly unchanged compared to Gaussian likelihood, with less than 5% variation in figure of merit across different settings and statistics. No detectable skewness appears on intermediate scales in realistic Euclid mocks due to shot noise.
AI.conclusion: The Gaussian likelihood assumption is robust for Euclid 2-point statistics analyses in both Fourier and configuration spaces, even considering skewness via Edgeworth expansion.

title: Smoluchowski Coagulation Equation and the Evolution of Primordial Black Hole Clusters
summary: In arXiv:2507.07171, we demonstrate that the high-redshift supermassive black holes in the so-called "little red dots" discovered by James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) can be explained by the primordial black hole (PBH) clustering on small scales. In this paper, we present a comprehensive simulation of the successive PBH mergers within a cluster by solving the Smoluchowski coagulation equation. We derive the coagulation kernel considering both cases with and without the effects of mass segregation. Then we employ the Monte Carlo method to solve the equation, implementing the full-conditioning scheme using the discrete inverse transformation method. Our simulations determine the runaway timescales of clusters and the mass population evolution of PBHs across a wide range of cosmic redshifts, depending on the number of PBHs within the cluster and the associated density.

AI.tldr: This paper models the merger-driven growth of primordial black holes in clusters to explain high-redshift supermassive black holes detected by JWST, using coagulation equations and Monte Carlo simulations to track their mass evolution over time.
AI.motivation: To explain the high-redshift supermassive black holes observed by JWST through primordial black hole clustering.
AI.method: Simulation of primordial black hole mergers using the Smoluchowski coagulation equation, deriving coagulation kernels with and without mass segregation effects, and solving via Monte Carlo with full-conditioning and discrete inverse transformation.
AI.result: Determination of runaway merger timescales and mass evolution of primordial black holes in clusters across cosmic redshifts, contingent on cluster size and density.
AI.conclusion: Primordial black hole clustering and successive mergers can account for the early formation of supermassive black holes observed as "little red dots" by JWST.

title: Cosmological Constraints on the Generalized Uncertainty Principle from Redshift-Space Distortions
summary: We investigate the imprints of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle on cosmological scales by using redshift-space distortion measurements in combination with background cosmological data to determine constraints on the deformation parameter $β$. We consider the modified Poisson bracket related to the existence of a minimal length, which leads to a modified Raychaudhuri equation for the standard $Λ$CDM model and gives rise to a phenomenological one-parameter dynamical dark energy scenario. Through this modification, we can reveal the effects of the minimal length on the late-time structure of the universe. We employ the $f$ and $fσ_8$ measurements of the growth rate combined with background data, including cosmic chronometers, baryon acoustic oscillations and Type Ia supernova observations. The observational constraints reveal a systematically negative value for the deformation parameter $β$, with the $Λ$CDM limit lying within the 95\% credible interval. When supernova data are included, the Akaike Information Criterion indicates weak-to-strong support in favour of the GUP-modified model depending on the SNIa catalogue, while the Bayesian evidence suggests a weak preference.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle on cosmology by modifying ΛCDM dynamics and constraining the related deformation parameter β using multiple datasets, finding indications of minimal length effects and some observational preference for the modified model.
AI.motivation: To explore the cosmological implications of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP), particularly how a minimal length affects late-time universe structure and dark energy dynamics.
AI.method: Used redshift-space distortion measurements combined with background cosmological data (cosmic chronometers, BAO, Type Ia supernovae) to constrain the deformation parameter β in a modified ΛCDM model incorporating a modified Poisson bracket and Raychaudhuri equation reflecting GUP effects.
AI.result: Constraints indicate a systematically negative deformation parameter β with the ΛCDM limit within the 95% credible interval. Model comparisons show weak-to-strong support for the GUP-modified model when supernova data are included, with Bayesian evidence favoring it weakly.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals measurable imprints of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle on cosmological scales, suggesting that minimal length effects can influence late-time universe dynamics and dark energy behavior, with observational data providing tentative support for this extension of the ΛCDM model.

title: Estimates of the Dynamic Characteristics of Binary Systems for Traversable Wormholes Search
summary: The work is devoted to the study of the possibilities of observational manifestations of traversable wormholes (WHs). The simplest binary system model consisting of a traversable WH candidate (black hole (BH), supermassive BH) and a companion star, whose motion is perturbed by a massive object (star) located on the other side of the wormhole throat, is considered. In the first case of supermassive BH as WH candidate the perturbing acceleration is analyzed and compared with a competing effect in the form of the stochastic influence of stars adjacent to the companion star. In the second case the features of the change in the radial velocity of the companion star in the model of a wide binary system with a WH are also analyzed in order to distinguish it from the following models: 1) a binary system with a BH, and 2) a triple system. For the observational accuracy in radial velocity expected in the near future, at the level of 1.5 km/s the radial velocity perturbations are detectable for all considered observation time spans. For a more realistic accuracy of 10 km/s, the spectral analysis methods become statistically significant after approximately 17 years of data accumulation. The application of spectral and non-parametric methods significantly decreases the required accumulation time compared to matched-filtering applied in isolation.

AI.tldr: This study models binary star systems with traversable wormholes to identify observational signatures that differentiate them from black holes or triple systems, finding that radial velocity perturbations are detectable with upcoming instruments using advanced data analysis techniques over realistic timescales.
AI.motivation: To investigate observational signatures of traversable wormholes by analyzing their influence on binary star systems, enabling distinction from black holes and triple systems.
AI.method: Modeling binary systems with a traversable wormhole candidate and companion star; analyzing perturbation in companion star's motion and radial velocity; comparing with stochastic stellar influences and models of BH binaries and triple systems; applying spectral and non-parametric data analysis methods to simulated radial velocity data over time.
AI.result: Radial velocity perturbations caused by a wormhole are detectable with near-future observational accuracy (1.5 km/s) over practical timescales; at 10 km/s accuracy, significant detection requires about 17 years of data, which can be shortened using spectral and non-parametric methods versus matched-filtering alone.
AI.conclusion: Observational manifestations of traversable wormholes in binary systems may be distinguished from black hole or triple system scenarios through detailed analysis of radial velocity perturbations, with spectral and non-parametric techniques enhancing detectability within feasible observation periods.

title: Low-mass failed supernovae and the $10\,M_{\odot}$ peak in the merging black hole mass distribution
summary: Gravitational-wave observations reveal that the rate of merging black holes drops by $\sim2$ orders of magnitude from component masses $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ to $\sim 15\,M_{\odot}$. The increased compactness of the black hole progenitor cores may contribute to the $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ overdensity, but cannot fully explain the rate difference. In this paper, we consider the possibility that the overdensity is reinforced by supernova processes that result in efficient black hole formation from direct collapse in a narrow range around $10\, M_{\odot}$. We extend previous studies by considering a distinct subpopulation of failed-supernovae black holes, possibly separated by a gap in the primary mass distribution from the rest of the population. Using 153 observations from the latest GWTC-4.0 catalog, we confirm a strong peak in the primary mass distribution at $10\,M_{\odot}$, with a peak rate density of $7.36_{-3.11}^{+6.35}$ $M_{\odot}^{-1}\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}$. The rate drops sharply and becomes consistent with zero at the 90 % level for primary mass $m_1\in (12.0, 16.1)\, M_{\odot}$, then rises again to confidently nonzero values above $\sim 16\,M_{\odot}$ before falling at higher masses. Our results reveal structure in the mass distribution in the $10-20\,M_{\odot}$ range, with rate changes of multiple orders of magnitude across a few solar masses, consistent with a distinct population of failed-supernova black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper finds evidence for a distinct population of black holes formed by failed supernovae, causing a peak at 10 solar masses and a gap between 12-16.1 solar masses in the merger rate distribution from gravitational-wave data.
AI.motivation: Gravitational-wave observations show a significant drop in merging black hole rates between ~10 and ~15 solar masses, which is not fully explained by progenitor core compactness.
AI.method: Analyzed 153 observations from the GWTC-4.0 catalog, considering a distinct subpopulation of failed-supernovae black holes and examining the primary mass distribution for evidence of a gap and overdensity around 10 solar masses.
AI.result: Confirmed a strong peak in the primary mass distribution at 10 solar masses with a high rate density, a sharp drop to near zero rate between 12-16.1 solar masses, then a rise again beyond ~16 solar masses, indicating a distinct failed-supernova black hole population.
AI.conclusion: The observed mass distribution structure between 10-20 solar masses, characterized by abrupt rate changes, supports the existence of a separate population of black holes formed via failed supernovae direct collapse, reinforcing the overdensity around 10 solar masses.

title: No evidence for dynamical dark energy from the Combo correlation of GRBs
summary: Recently, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) collaboration has presented results indicating that dark energy may exhibit dynamical behavior. Calibrated gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations can be employed to verify or reject a time-evolution of the dark energy (DE) equation of state, $ω(z)$, up to redshifts $z\sim 9$. We use the most updated catalog of GRBs fulfilling the Combo correlation and improve its calibration employing three catalogs of type Ia supernovae at redshifts $z\leq0.075$ and the Bézier interpolation of the Hubble rate, as an alternative to the cosmographic series that fails to be constraining at high redshifts. To test the evolution of $ω(z)$, we adopt a model-independent, redshift-binned DE parametrization. In both the calibration and the DE reconstruction analyses the impact of the spatial curvature on the results is explored. The calibrated Combo correlation yields a Hubble constant $H_0\sim70$ km/s/Mpc which alleviates the existing Hubble tension and is broadly consistent with current measurements, although the uncertainties prevent a high-precision measurement. Regarding the reconstruction of $ω(z)$ of DE, spatially curved scenarios are disfavored and, despite the apparent ''phantom'' behavior at $z\lesssim0.55$ due to the limited statistics caused by the shortage of nearby events, at $z>0.55$ the analysis provides statistically robust evidence in favor of the cosmological constant scenario. The Combo correlation alleviates the Hubble tension and shows no significant evidence in favor of dynamical DE. This suggests that GRBs, as distance indicators, are broadly consistent with the current cosmic distance ladder.

AI.tldr: This study calibrates gamma-ray bursts using supernova data and Bézier interpolation to test dark energy evolution up to redshift 9. It finds a Hubble constant near 70 km/s/Mpc, lessening Hubble tension, disfavors spatial curvature, and finds no strong evidence for dynamical dark energy, supporting the cosmological constant model.
AI.motivation: To investigate the possible dynamical behavior of dark energy and verify or reject time-evolution of the dark energy equation of state, extending measurements to high redshifts using gamma-ray bursts as cosmological probes.
AI.method: Utilized the updated gamma-ray burst catalog calibrated with type Ia supernovae catalogs and Bézier interpolation of the Hubble rate to bypass limitations of cosmographic series, combined with a model-independent, redshift-binned dark energy parametrization and analysis of spatial curvature effects.
AI.result: The calibrated Combo correlation yields a Hubble constant around 70 km/s/Mpc, alleviating the Hubble tension; spatial curvature is disfavored; evolutionary signs of dark energy equation of state are not statistically significant beyond low redshift 'phantom' behavior; results support consistency with the cosmological constant scenario.
AI.conclusion: Gamma-ray bursts calibrated via the Combo correlation provide Hubble constant measurements that ease the Hubble tension and support a cosmological constant model of dark energy, showing no robust evidence for its dynamical evolution, and are consistent with the established cosmic distance ladder.

title: Insights from GRBs for optical follow-up of gravitational wave counterparts
summary: Identifying the electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave sources is vital to enabling the myriad of investigations possible with multimessenger astronomy. However, locating faint, fast-varying transients within large localisations remains challenging given the uncertainty in their detailed properties. In this work, we investigate how the nearby merger-induced GRBs would be localised by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detector network during the fifth gravitational wave observing run (O5) and assess whether their optical counterparts could be detected using gravitational wave localisations alone, without additional localisation from gamma-ray instruments. Counterpart detectability is evaluated using the observed optical afterglow lightcurves of these GRBs and the distance-scaled lightcurve of the kilonova AT2017gfo as a fiducial template. We find that such events can be localised to comparatively small regions of the sky, often only a few to tens of square degrees. As a result, counterparts are detectable by at least one of the available optical telescopes during O5. However, detectability depends strongly on observational depth, as the counterparts are fainter than $22$ mag within a day. Facilities capable of reaching depths of $\gtrsim23$ mag therefore play a key role in recovering these faint counterparts. These results indicate that for such events during O5, the primary challenge for multimessenger discovery will be in achieving sufficient observational depth and reliably identifying the true counterpart among unrelated transients rather than gravitational wave localisation itself.

AI.tldr: This study shows that during the O5 gravitational wave run, nearby GRBs' optical counterparts can be localized within small sky areas and detected with sufficiently deep optical observations (≥23 mag), shifting the primary challenge to achieving observational depth and correct transient identification rather than localization precision.
AI.motivation: To explore the challenge of identifying electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave sources, specifically nearby merger-induced GRBs, to enhance multimessenger astronomy investigations.
AI.method: Simulating localization of nearby GRBs by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network during the fifth observing run (O5) and assessing optical counterpart detectability using observed GRB afterglow lightcurves and kilonova lightcurve templates.
AI.result: Nearby GRBs can be localized to small sky regions (few to tens of square degrees), and their optical counterparts are detectable by optical telescopes during O5 if sufficient observational depth (≥23 mag) is achieved.
AI.conclusion: The main difficulty in multimessenger discovery of nearby merger-induced GRBs during O5 lies in reaching adequate observational depth and accurately distinguishing true counterparts from unrelated transients, rather than the gravitational wave localization itself.

title: Non-minimally coupled quintessence with sign-switching interaction
summary: We propose a new non-minimally coupled quintessence model to account for the late-time dark energy dynamics indicated by recent DESI measurements. Within this framework, the quintessence density begins to decrease only when it starts to dominate the universe, which naturally accounts for the late-time onset of dark energy weakening. The coupling also induces a sign change in the effective energy transfer between dark matter and dark energy during cosmic evolution. While the scalar field itself remains canonical and never crosses the phantom divide, the modified evolution of the dark matter density gives rise to an effective crossing behavior in the observationally inferred dark energy sector. Compared with both $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM models, our model is favored more strongly by current cosmological data. This work may provide a promising avenue for understanding the observational late-time weakening of dark energy and the origin of its dynamics.

AI.tldr: A new non-minimally coupled quintessence model explains the late-time weakening of dark energy observed by DESI, showing energy transfer sign changes with dark matter and outperforming standard ΛCDM models in data fitting.
AI.motivation: To address and explain the late-time dark energy dynamics and weakening observed in recent DESI measurements, which are not fully accounted for in standard cosmological models.
AI.method: Propose a novel non-minimally coupled quintessence model wherein quintessence density decreases only after dominance, inducing a sign change in energy transfer between dark matter and dark energy without crossing the phantom divide by the scalar field itself.
AI.result: The model naturally explains the late-time onset of dark energy weakening and exhibits an effective crossing behavior of dark energy when inferred observationally; it is favored over the ΛCDM and w₀wₐCDM models by current cosmological data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed non-minimally coupled quintessence model provides a robust theoretical framework for the observed late-time weakening of dark energy and offers insight into its dynamic origin, presenting a promising alternative to standard dark energy models.

title: Impacts of Voids, Line of Sight Interactions, and Local Emission Environment on Detectability of Gamma-Ray AGN
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary:
Cosmic voids may have novel affects on the propagation of high-energy photons. We consider the fraction of the line of sight that intersect voids (termed \enquote{voidiness}). A previous study showed that active galactic nuclei (AGN) detected by \textit{Fermi} Large Area Telescope (LAT) lie along voidier lines of sight than redshift-matched populations of Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optically detected quasars in the redshift range from $0.4 \leq z < 0.7$.
  We explore this difference and various astrophysical explanations for it. Weaker intergalactic magnetic fields in voids would naturally enhance the gamma-ray cascading flux within the \textit{Fermi}-LAT point-spread function. We find that line-of-sight interactions increasing the flux in the \textit{Fermi}-LAT energy band by $\sim$0.1\% per Mpc of void traversed may be sufficient to result in the observed difference in voidiness distributions. Voidiness comparisons between SDSS QSO and AGN detected by imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at very-high-energies (VHE) do not yield any conclusive statement, likely because of the limited VHE sample size, and therefore are inconclusive about the role of possibly weaker extragalactic background light within voids. Finally, we measure that $28 \pm 3 \%$ of gamma-ray detected sources exist within a void (consistent with random mock populations) compared to $19.1 \pm 0.3 \%$ of SDSS quasars. We do not find any significant local void effect for gamma-ray sources that would explain the voidiness difference between \textit{Fermi}-LAT gamma-ray and SDSS QSO sources. These results suggest that the observed difference in voidiness distributions may be due to line-of-sight interactions rather than the local emission environment of gamma-ray AGN.

AI.tldr: High-energy gamma-ray sources detected by Fermi-LAT tend to lie along lines of sight intersecting more cosmic voids than optical quasars, likely because weak magnetic fields in voids enhance gamma-ray flux during propagation rather than differences in their local environments.
AI.motivation: To investigate the impact of cosmic voids on the propagation of high-energy photons and to understand why active galactic nuclei (AGN) detected by Fermi-LAT lie along voidier sightlines than redshift-matched SDSS quasars.
AI.method: Analyzing the fraction of line of sight intersecting cosmic voids ('voidiness'), comparing voidiness distributions between gamma-ray detected AGN and SDSS quasars, and considering astrophysical mechanisms such as weaker intergalactic magnetic fields and line-of-sight interactions enhancing gamma-ray flux; also comparing with very-high-energy AGN data and simulating random distributions.
AI.result: The study finds that a small increase (~0.1% per Mpc) in gamma-ray flux due to line-of-sight interactions through voids can explain the higher voidiness of Fermi-LAT AGN compared to SDSS quasars. There is no significant local void effect on gamma-ray sources. The fraction of gamma-ray detected sources within voids matches random expectations, suggesting the voidiness difference arises from propagation effects rather than source environments.
AI.conclusion: The observed difference in voidiness between gamma-ray AGN and optically selected quasars is likely caused by line-of-sight interactions enhancing gamma-ray flux in voids, not by local void effects around gamma-ray sources.

title: Consistency relations of amplitude and phase fluctuations of gravitational waves magnified by strong gravitational lensing
summary: We discuss the amplitude and phase fluctuations of gravitational waves due to wave optics lensing in the presence of both a strong lens and cosmological weak lenses. By applying the geometric optics approximation to the strong lens and treating the weak lensing potential perturbatively, we obtain the amplification factor up to the second order in the weak lensing potential. Additionally, we establish a methodology to systematically evaluate the weak lensing effects based on diagrammatic rules. Based on the derived amplification factor, we evaluate the statistics of the fluctuations and demonstrate that the consistency relations originally established in the absence of a strong lens still hold in exactly the same form when a strong lens is present. The physical origin of these relations is also discussed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for the mean of the weak lensing signal, both the magnification of the signal and the shift of the Fresnel scale to larger scales occur, consistent with the behavior observed in the variance.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes gravitational wave fluctuations caused by strong and weak lensing using geometric optics and perturbation theory, deriving an amplification factor that respects known consistency relations and shows new effects on magnification and Fresnel scale shifts.
AI.motivation: To understand how gravitational waves are affected by combined strong and weak lensing, particularly the amplitude and phase fluctuations due to wave optics effects.
AI.method: Applying geometric optics approximation for the strong lens and perturbative treatment for cosmological weak lenses to derive the amplification factor to second order; additionally, introducing a diagrammatic method to systematically evaluate weak lensing effects.
AI.result: Derived amplification factor including second-order weak lensing effects; established consistency relations hold even with a strong lens; showed the mean weak lensing signal exhibits magnification and Fresnel scale shifts matching variance behavior.
AI.conclusion: The interplay between strong and weak lensing on gravitational waves can be systematically described, preserving known consistency relations and revealing coherent physical effects including magnification and Fresnel scale shifts in the weak lensing statistics.

title: The impact of the eROSITA bubbles on Galactic cosmic-ray transport
summary: We propose that the observed spectral hardening in Galactic cosmic ray fluxes is governed by macroscopic Galactic outflows, such as the eROSITA bubbles, rather than microphysical variations in their scattering properties. Employing a phenomenological transport model, we show that an advective outflow boundary naturally reproduces the $300\,$GV hardening in secondary-to-primary ratios. Global fits to precision AMS-02 data yield an effective local inner halo boundary of $\sim 5\,$kpc and an outflow speed of $\sim 360\,$km/s, in striking agreement with independent multi-wavelength kinematic constraints of the eROSITA outflows. This interpretation provides a testable alternative to breaks in the effective diffusion coefficient, without increasing the number of free parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper explains cosmic ray spectral hardening by Galactic outflows modeled phenomenologically, fitting AMS-02 data well and aligning with independent outflow observations, suggesting a viable alternative to diffusion-based interpretations.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed spectral hardening in Galactic cosmic ray fluxes without relying on microphysical variations in scattering properties.
AI.method: Using a phenomenological transport model incorporating macroscopic Galactic outflows (e.g., eROSITA bubbles) and fitting global precision AMS-02 data.
AI.result: The model naturally reproduces the 300 GV hardening in secondary-to-primary ratios and yields an effective local inner halo boundary of ~5 kpc and outflow speed of ~360 km/s, consistent with independent kinematic data.
AI.conclusion: Spectral hardening in Galactic cosmic ray fluxes can be attributed to large-scale advective Galactic outflows rather than changes in diffusion properties, providing a testable and parameter-economical alternative explanation.

title: Revealing the neutrino mass through persistent homology of the cosmic web
summary: Cosmological constraints on neutrino mass offer a promising avenue for advancing our understanding of both fundamental particle physics and the evolution of cosmic large-scale structure. To overcome challenges associated with traditional probes of neutrino mass, particularly degeneracies with other parameters, we consider topological summaries of the cosmic web based on the formalism of persistent homology. We introduce persistence strips, a novel representation that segments Betti curves by topological persistence, effectively condensing two-dimensional persistence diagrams into a set of one-dimensional curves. Applied to the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations, these topological descriptors demonstrate pronounced sensitivity to neutrino mass. By constructing an emulator spanning a 10-dimensional $w_0 w_a\text{CDM} +ν$ cosmological parameter space that includes parameters degenerate with neutrino masses in conventional approaches, assuming a volume of only $(350 \, \mathrm{Mpc})^3$, we obtain neutrino mass constraints with an uncertainty of $0.05 \, \mathrm{eV}$ for the total matter field and $0.13 \, \mathrm{eV}$ for the dark matter-only field, with the strongest constraints coming from void topology. Persistence strips exhibit roughly twice the constraining power of unbinned Betti curves and, through their multi-scale, environment-dependent sensitivity, systematically break degeneracies between neutrino mass and other cosmological parameters. We pinpoint the precise physical origin of the signal, identifying two equally important contributions: sensitivity to the neutrino mass fraction, which is highest in underdense regions, and the impact of neutrinos on the distribution of dark matter. Our findings highlight the particular promise of applying topological statistics to weak lensing measurements, which directly probe the total matter distribution.

AI.tldr: This paper leverages a novel topological data analysis technique, persistence strips, applied to cosmological simulations to improve constraints on neutrino mass, overcoming traditional degeneracies and highlighting the promising role of topology in cosmic structure studies.
AI.motivation: Traditional cosmological probes of neutrino mass face challenges due to parameter degeneracies, limiting their effectiveness in constraining neutrino mass and understanding its impact on cosmic structure.
AI.method: The paper introduces persistence strips, a topological summary technique that segments Betti curves by topological persistence, converting 2D persistence diagrams into 1D curves. These are applied to the FLAMINGO cosmological simulations and used to build an emulator over a 10-dimensional cosmological parameter space including neutrino mass and degenerate parameters.
AI.result: Persistence strips yield significantly improved sensitivity to neutrino mass, achieving uncertainties of 0.05 eV for total matter and 0.13 eV for dark matter-only fields. They outperform unbinned Betti curves by roughly a factor of two and break degeneracies through multi-scale and environment-specific sensitivity. The strongest constraints come from void topology.
AI.conclusion: Topological statistics based on persistent homology, particularly persistence strips, provide a powerful new approach to constrain neutrino mass in cosmology. They effectively isolate signals from neutrino mass and associated effects, particularly in underdense regions, and are promising for application to weak lensing observations probing total matter distribution.

title: The Real and Pseudo Dispersion Measures of FRB~20220912A
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients. As they propagate through the interstellar medium, they interact with free electrons, resulting in dispersion. The corresponding dispersion measure (DM) is referred to as the real DM (DM$_{\rm real}$). In practice, however, the dispersion measure derived from modeling (DM$_{\rm model}$) is often contaminated by intrinsic burst morphology, giving rise to a pseudo DM component (DM$_{\rm pseudo} = {\rm DM}_{\rm model} - {\rm DM}_{\rm real}$). In this work, we focus on the highly active repeating FRB~20220912A and utilize its microshots -- extremely short-duration (typically tens of microseconds), broadband emissions -- to investigate its DM$_{\rm real}$ and DM$_{\rm pseudo}$. We adopt two assumptions: first, that FRB~20220912A resides in a non-magneto-ionic environment and that its DM$_{\rm real}$ variation is smaller than $10^{-2}$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ over a few years; and second, that microshots have a negligible intrinsic morphological time delay. By identifying two new microshots and combining them with previously reported ones, we find that all four microshots exhibit remarkably consistent DM values over a one-month timescale, with an average of $219.380 \pm 0.004\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$. We define this value as the DM$_{\rm real}$ of FRB~20220912A. We further show that bright, narrow bursts with a width of less than 2\,ms also yield DM estimates consistent with the microshot-based DM$_{\rm real}$. A survey of five repeating FRBs reveals that DM$_{\rm pseudo}$ is a common phenomenon, with variations typically spanning a range of approximately $10\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ at 1.2\,GHz. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for morphological contributions in DM interpretation and demonstrate that microshots and narrow bursts are powerful tools for probing DM$_{\rm real}$.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that intrinsic burst morphology contaminates modeled dispersion measures in fast radio bursts, but short-duration microshots and narrow bursts can reliably measure the real dispersion measure, revealing significant pseudo DM variations in repeating FRBs.
AI.motivation: To accurately determine the real dispersion measure (DM_real) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by addressing contamination from intrinsic burst morphology in the modeled DM (DM_model), which introduces a pseudo DM component (DM_pseudo).
AI.method: Focused on repeating FRB 20220912A, utilized extremely short-duration microshots with negligible intrinsic time delay. Assumed a stable, non-magneto-ionic environment and minimal variation in DM_real over years. Identified and combined new microshots with existing ones to measure consistent DM values. Conducted a survey of five repeating FRBs to assess the prevalence of DM_pseudo.
AI.result: The average DM_real for FRB 20220912A was determined as 219.380 ± 0.004 pc cm^-3, consistent across microshots and narrow bursts under 2 ms. The study found that DM_pseudo commonly affects repeating FRBs, causing variations up to ~10 pc cm^-3. Microshots and narrow bursts serve as effective probes to distinguish DM_real from DM_pseudo.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic burst morphology can significantly bias dispersion measure estimates in FRBs, leading to a pseudo DM component. Using microshots and narrow bursts allows robust measurement of the real DM, improving interpretation of FRB propagation effects. Accounting for DM_pseudo is crucial for accurate FRB studies.

title: Gaussian Process Inference of Stochastic Magneto-Active Dynamics and Viscosity in Swift J1727.8-1613
summary: Linking X-ray variability to the underlying magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics of black hole X-ray binaries remains challenging. We systematically investigate the stochastic and oscillatory variability of the black hole X-ray binary candidate Swift J1727.8$-$1613 during its 2023 outburst using Gaussian process (GP) regression applied to Insight-HXMT multi-band light curves. The variability is modeled with a physically motivated composite kernel comprising one stochastically driven damped simple harmonic oscillator (SHO) and two damped random walk (DRW) components. The SHO term robustly recovers quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) with frequencies $ν_0 \sim 0.07$--$5$ Hz, consistent with the fundamental Alfvén mode of a contracting magnetically confined disk--coronal cavity. The quality factor rises from $Q \sim 3$ to $Q \sim 10$, suggesting increasing coherence of the magnetic cavity. We also find an anti-correlation between QPO frequency and the short DRW damping timescale, supporting our proposed stochastic magneto-active dynamics scenario. Associating the short and long DRW timescales with the local turbulent turnover and thermal adjustment timescales, respectively, we infer an effective viscosity parameter of $α\approx 0.1$, supporting a strongly magnetized accretion flow. Strikingly, near the onset of relativistic jet ejection around MJD 60206, both relaxation timescales collapse toward the 0.1 s sampling limit, suggesting a rapid reorganization of the disk internal energy balance immediately before jet launching. Our results establish GP inference as a powerful route to connecting X-ray timing observables with the dynamical state of black hole accretion flows.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Gaussian process regression on X-ray data of Swift J1727.8-1613 to model variability via damped oscillators and random walks, revealing magnetic cavity dynamics, accretion flow viscosity, and disk changes preceding jet ejection, demonstrating GP's power in astrophysical timing analysis.
AI.motivation: To link X-ray variability with the underlying magnetohydrodynamic dynamics in black hole X-ray binaries, which is challenging due to complex physical processes.
AI.method: Used Gaussian process regression with a composite kernel combining a stochastically driven damped simple harmonic oscillator and two damped random walk components on multi-band light curves from Insight-HXMT.
AI.result: Recovered quasi-periodic oscillations consistent with Alfvén modes, observed increasing coherence in the magnetic cavity, found anti-correlation between QPO frequency and damping timescale, inferred viscosity parameter supporting strongly magnetized accretion flow, and observed rapid disk reorganization before jet ejection.
AI.conclusion: GP regression effectively connects X-ray timing variability with magnetohydrodynamic processes in black hole accretion flows, providing insights into disk dynamics and jet launching mechanisms.

title: GECAM discovery of a peculiar magnetar X-ray burst (MXB 221120) from SGR J1935+2154 associated with a fast radio burst
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are enigmatic cosmic transients of millisecond duration observed in the radio band. The identification of FRB-associated magnetar X-ray bursts (MXBs) from galactic magnetar SGR J1935+2154 suggests that at least a fraction of FRBs can be produced from magnetar activity. However, the sample size of FRB-associated MXBs is still very small. Here we report a bright and peculiar FRB-associated MXB from SGR J1935+2154 detected by GECAM on November 20, 2022, dubbed MXB 221120. We find that both temporal and spectral properties of MXB 221120 exhibit distinctive features. Its light curve could be generally described by a single FRED function with superposition of several narrow pulses. Interestingly, we identify a possible QPO feature with center frequency of ~18 Hz in this MXB. The time-integrated spectrum is best fitted by a blackbody model with temperature (kT ) of 18.6 keV, rendering it the first thermal spectrum FRB-associated MXB from SGR J1935+2154. Compared to other MXBs with single emission episode, MXB 221120 has longer duration and higher blackbody temperature, making it an outlier in the burst sample. These results indicate that MXB 221120 may be produced by a special mechanism with extreme physical conditions.

AI.tldr: A new FRB-associated X-ray burst (MXB 221120) from magnetar SGR J1935+2154 exhibits unique thermal spectral and temporal properties, suggesting an uncommon physical mechanism behind its production.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature of FRB-associated magnetar X-ray bursts (MXBs) and increase the limited sample size of such events, enhancing understanding of their physical mechanisms.
AI.method: Detection and analysis of a bright FRB-associated MXB from SGR J1935+2154 using GECAM data, including temporal, spectral analysis, and identification of light curve features such as FRED function fitting and quasi-periodic oscillations (QPO).
AI.result: Identification of MXB 221120 with a unique thermal spectrum modeled by blackbody radiation at 18.6 keV, a longer duration, higher temperature, and a possible ~18 Hz QPO, indicating distinctive physical conditions compared to other MXBs.
AI.conclusion: MXB 221120 represents a peculiar FRB-associated magnetar X-ray burst produced by a special mechanism under extreme physical conditions, expanding the diversity of known FRB-associated MXBs and offering new insights into their origins.

title: Magneto-Active Environments in Pulsar Binaries with the MeerKAT Telescope: I. Pulsar sample and their basic properties
summary: Eclipsing pulsar binaries and binaries with a high mass companion are ideal systems for studying and understanding the properties of plasma in magneto-ionic environments. In this work, the first paper of a series, we present MeerKAT observations of three pulsar binaries: the high-mass binary PSR J1740$-$3052, the black widow PSR J2051$-$0827 and the redback PSR J1748$-$2446A (Terzan~5A). With the help of MeerKAT's high-sensitivity polarimetric observations, we characterise the properties of these sources, including the linear/circular polarization, dispersion measure (DM), rotation measure (RM) and scattering time. The two eclipsing millisecond pulsars exhibit strong orbital-phase-dependent propagation effects and we observe $\sim$2 eclipses in these systems during our observations. PSR J1740$-$3052 is a binary system with a 231 d orbital period. The relatively large separation results in a smooth RM variation, enabling us to resolve its variation timescale and constrain the small-scale magnetic structure. A gradual RM variation is observed over $\sim$1500 s, occurring near periastron. This behaviour implies a magnetic spatial scale of $\sim$0.003 AU in the companion wind, assuming a relative velocity of $\sim$250 km s$^{-1}$. The linear polarisation intensity profiles of PSR J2051$-$0827 show shape variations as a function of frequency, with a stronger leading component emerging at lower frequencies. We observe signatures of the propagation effect in the polarisation properties of PSR J1748$-$2446A during eclipse ingress and egress. This could arise from Faraday Conversion or multipath propagation of the pulsar signal and requires detailed analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper presents high-sensitivity MeerKAT polarimetric observations of three pulsar binaries, revealing detailed plasma propagation effects, frequency-dependent polarization changes, and magnetic field structures in their magneto-ionic environments.
AI.motivation: To study and understand plasma properties in magneto-ionic environments using eclipsing pulsar binaries and binaries with high mass companions as ideal systems.
AI.method: MeerKAT's high-sensitivity polarimetric observations were used to characterize polarization properties, dispersion measure, rotation measure, and scattering time of three pulsar binaries: PSR J1740-3052, PSR J2051-0827, and PSR J1748-2446A.
AI.result: Observed orbital-phase-dependent propagation effects, including eclipses in millisecond pulsars. PSR J1740-3052 showed smooth RM variations near periastron allowing constraints on small-scale magnetic structures. PSR J2051-0827 displayed frequency-dependent linear polarization profile changes. PSR J1748-2446A exhibited polarization propagation effects during eclipse ingress and egress, possibly due to Faraday Conversion or multipath propagation.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully characterized the magneto-ionic plasma environments around these pulsar binaries using detailed polarimetric observations, revealing small-scale magnetic structures and complex polarization propagation effects related to their orbital phases and companion winds.
